excerpts:
Just as the Children of the Light are focused on fighting servants of the Dark One, the Scarlet Crusade are focused on fighting undead and both are colloquially referred to with their color scheme ("Scarlets" for the Scarlet Crusade and "Whitecloaks" for the Children of Light). There's even a plot point where the Whitecloaks' leader was a Darkfriend, inspiring how in WoW their leader was a Dreadlord (no relation to the Dreadlords from A Wheel of Time) in disguise. Their descent to villainy could also draw inspiration from on negative accounts and stereotypes of those real-life organizations.

[Home](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/) › [Game Logos](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/category/inspiration/graphic-design/logos/video-game/) › The World Of Warcraft Logo History, Colors, Font, And Meaning

# The World Of Warcraft Logo History, Colors, Font, And Meaning

[Bogdan Sandu](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/author/bogdanel/) Designer & Founder

27 December 2025

17 min read

The World Of Warcraft Logo History, Colors, Font, And Meaning

The **World of Warcraft logo** is one of the most recognized visual identities in gaming history. It represents Blizzard Entertainment’s flagship MMORPG, which launched in 2004 and changed online gaming permanently. The logo combines aggressive fantasy [typography](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-typography/) with a color palette built around deep blues, golds, and blacks, making it instantly recognizable across merchandise, digital platforms, and expansion packaging worldwide.

...

* **Design Type:** Wordmark with ornamental typographic treatment
* **Primary Elements:** Stylized letterforms, decorative serifs, metallic color effects, and a stacked two-line text layout (“World of Warcraft”)
* **Official Introduction Date:** 2004, alongside the game’s original release on November 23, 2004
* **Designer/Agency:** Blizzard Entertainment’s in-house art team
* **Trademark Status:** Registered trademark owned by Blizzard Entertainment (Activision Blizzard)
* **Color Palette:** Deep navy blue (), metallic gold (), and black () as the base
* **Usage Context:** Game packaging, expansion branding, in-game UI, merchandise, marketing materials, and digital storefronts

## How Has the World of Warcraft Logo Evolved Over Time?

World of Warcraft logo

...

* **Design Description:** Core WoW wordmark retained, with expansion subtitle added in a complementary style using red and orange tones to signal a more aggressive, demonic theme
* **Color Scheme:** Gold base with added crimson and ember tones in the expansion title
* **Designer:** Blizzard Entertainment
* **Context:** First major expansion, introducing Outland and the Burning Legion as central antagonists
* **Key Changes from Previous:** Introduction of expansion subtitle system that would define all future WoW branding
* **Cultural Significance:** Established the visual pattern of pairing the core logo with thematically distinct expansion wordmarks

### Wrath of the Lich King Logo (2008)

* **Years Active:** 2008–2010
* **Design Description:** Ice-blue tones dominated the expansion subtitle, with frost texture effects applied to the lettering
* **Color Scheme:** Ice blue, silver, dark blue
* **Designer:** Blizzard Entertainment

...

The gold-on-dark treatment echoes medieval heraldry and illuminated manuscripts, which fits Azeroth’s lore-heavy world-building approach.

There’s also a subtle connection to [Art Deco](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-art-deco-in-graphic-design/) sensibility in how the letters use decorative geometry without sacrificing legibility.

### Why Did Blizzard Choose These Specific Colors?

* **Metallic Gold ():** Signals prestige, legendary status, and reward. In WoW’s own UI, gold is the color of epic-tier loot, so the logo color and in-game [color psychology](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-color-psychology/) reinforce each other deliberately.
* **Navy Blue ():** Conveys depth, mystery, and arcane power. Blue is also the color of rare-quality items in the game’s loot system, creating another layer of brand-color alignment.
* **Black ():** Used as the base to maximize contrast and make the gold letterforms appear luminous.
Also grounds the design and prevents it from feeling too decorative.

The [color palette](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-color-palette/) works partly because it matches what players already associate with value and power inside the game itself. That kind of alignment between UI design and brand identity is harder to pull off than it looks.

### What Typography Style Is Used in the World of Warcraft Logo?

World of Warcraft logo

The [font](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-font/) used in the WoW logo is a custom typeface developed by Blizzard’s art team, not available commercially. It sits in the category of a decorative [display font](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-display-font/) with heavy fantasy ornamentation.

The letterforms feature high stroke contrast, prominent serifs with angled cuts, and subtle flaring at terminals that gives the text an almost hand-carved quality.

[Kerning](https://www.designyourway.

...

net/blog/gaming-company-logos/) broadly, Blizzard’s overall identity system is notable for using franchise-specific visual systems rather than a unified corporate aesthetic. WoW, Diablo, Overwatch, and StarCraft all look like they come from different branding universes, which is an unusual choice that somehow works.

## What Are the Technical Specifications of the World of Warcraft Logo?

### Official Color Codes

* **Primary Color: Metallic Gold**
* Hex: #C8A951
* [RGB](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-rgb/) : (200, 169, 81)
* [CMYK](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-cmyk/) : (0, 16, 60, 22)
* [Pantone](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-pantone/) : PMS 7406 C (approximate)
* **Secondary Color: Deep Navy Blue**
* Hex: #1A3A5C
* RGB: (26, 58, 92)
* CMYK: (72, 37, 0, 64)
* Pantone: PMS 2955 C (approximate)
* **Base Color: Black**
* Hex: #000000
* RGB: (0, 0, 0)
* CMYK: (0, 0, 0, 100)
* Pantone: Process Black C

...

Each layer connects back to the master wordmark visually while serving its own purpose.

The [brand guidelines](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-are-brand-guidelines/) that Blizzard shares with licensing partners treat the WoW logo as a master mark that must remain intact, with expansion subtitles functioning as secondary identifiers. This hierarchy is consistent across physical merchandise, digital platforms, and promotional materials.

The [brand style guide](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-brand-style-guide/) for WoW reportedly runs through approved color variations (full color, white knockout, black version), approved backgrounds, and clear usage restrictions. Partners who license the brand for physical merchandise go through Blizzard’s licensing team for asset access.

The logo also connects outward to Blizzard’s broader identity system, which includes the [Overwatch logo](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/overwatch-logo/) and the [Diablo logo](https://www.

...

It’s not commercially available. The letterforms are a heavily stylized fantasy [serif design](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-serif-font/) with exaggerated stroke contrast, ornate terminals, and a hand-carved quality that no off-the-shelf [typeface](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-a-typeface/) replicates exactly.

### What colors are in the World of Warcraft logo?

The primary colors are **metallic gold** (), deep navy blue (), and black ().

Each expansion subtitle introduces its own color treatment. Wrath of the Lich King used ice blue, while The Burning Crusade added crimson and ember tones. The master WoW wordmark itself stays consistent across all versions.

### Who designed the World of Warcraft logo?

Blizzard Entertainment’s in-house art team designed the logo, first introduced in 2004 alongside the game’s launch.

No single designer has been publicly credited.
The Warcraft franchise already had established visual language from earlier RTS titles, and the MMO logo was built as a heavier, more ornate evolution of that identity.

### Has the World of Warcraft logo ever changed?

The **core wordmark** has remained largely unchanged since 2004. Each expansion adds a distinct subtitle treatment with its own color palette and texture effects.

Later versions have been re-rendered at higher resolutions with improved detail work, but Blizzard has never fundamentally redesigned the master logo’s letterforms or structure.

### What does the World of Warcraft logo symbolize?

The ornate serif letterforms reference medieval manuscript traditions, signaling ancient history and epic scale.

The gold color connects directly to WoW’s in-game [color language](https://www.designyourway.net/blog/what-is-color-theory/) , where gold marks legendary-quality items. The dark background makes the lettering appear luminous.

...

The early Christian church adopted many of the symbols of the Roman Empire , including the importance of the color scarlet. After the Fall of Constantinople to the Turks in 1453, however, the imperial purple was no longer available, and Cardinals began instead to wear scarlet made from kermeses. ## Lore of the Scarlet Crusade

The Scarlet Crusade was created after the Third War, when a group of Silver Hand Paladins met in Southshore, in a secret meeting. They decided it was time to take care of the undead threat and cleanse the lands of Lordaeron once and for all. They agreed on a name and emblem - the Scarlet Crusade. The emblem was that of Lordaeron, only it was red - signifying the blood of those who gave their lives for Lordaeron.  
  
The founder was Saidan Dathrohan, who named himself Grand Crusader, along with his allies, he headed towards Heartglen, where they called all willing survivors to fight once more for the land they loved so much. A lot of people showed up, more than expected. The Scarlet Crusade was pure at that time, no strings attached.

...

He reformed the Scarlet Crusade into a new name, the Order of the Scarlet Flame, and togheter, they planned to take back New Avalon and Tyr's Hand from the Scourge forces, and after that... who knows...maybe even the Capital City itself.

World of Warcraft Forums

# Quest/Gossip frame background color and font color

Guides UI and Macro

[SilentNight-1046909](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/SilentNight-1046909) (SilentNight) August 15, 2019, 2:40am 1

Answered, thanks Ketho for telling me about **Immersion addon at curseforge.** (Forum not letting me post the curseforge link even though it let me post another link below.)  
So people can skip my wall of text now if they want. This thing converts the gossip windows into talking head windows that have white text on black background. (edit: mistakenly said it auto-accepts. It just accepts when you click on the dialog.) Just put it in the addon folder and runaway, no configuration needed.

Original post had some tips about gamma/brightness to see in difficult places too, down near the end, if anyone wants:
Hi, I have a glare sensitivity kind of issue where bright backgrounds washout dark text - about like trying to read the writing on a 200 watt light bulb that’s turned on. has anyone worked out how to flip the quest/gossip window’s background and font color scheme when talking to NPCs from dark font on gold background to light font on black background? I googled a lot and have encountered some RP gossip windows like tablets and shrines that have dark backgrounds and light text in their dialog windows when I interact with them. I’d love it if I could make all the human NPCs quest/gossip/dialog boxes have a dark background with light text.

I found this link on old EU forum post where someone provided code from scratch for an adhoc addon to adjust font sizes in the gossip frames independent of the rest of the UI.

[World of Warcraft Forums](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/)

### [World of Warcraft Forums](https://eu.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/)
The coder didn’t understand why black on gold would be hard to read and didn’t take a crack at that, but his other code would land people in the right place I think. At worst maybe a way to modify the font color to RGB code like 800 800 800 (or hex or whatever code the game uses for font colors). And for the background, since it’s a picture/image, maybe select the tablet gossip window background image instead of the npc gossip window background image or something like that.

Present workaround is alt-tab to wowhead. I’m not a hardcore RP’er super-bent on immersion, but-tabbing frequently still breaks the mood of the game a bit. Then the temptation to scroll down 2 more inches to see the final solutions in comments before trying to solve it myself…

Edit: also I’m pretty sure I’ve exhausted the in-game options like color blind mode and system-advanced-gamma/brightness/contrast stuff. Here are some cool settings I found in case anyone else feels a need-
**Those dark caves** \- System->Advanced gamma to max, brightness to about 30% give or take. I actually use this most everywhere and the topography on the minimap is quite nice.  
**Seeing tiny quest objects in the foggy swamp, desert or snow at high noon** \- brightness max, gamma very low. Monsters and terrain are shadowy, but those dumb little emerald shards in the one place or the tiny pearls in the other are visible for miles around! Just blindly tab-target 12345 the trash while getting those quest object. This also helped immensely with the minimap while in stormwind and with reading world maps in classic wow stress test. (Stormwind quite different in wow classic.) Flipping gamma and brightness back and forth every single time I talk to someone though… alt-tab to wowhead is preferable to that. Hoping to just find a way to customize the gossip box fonts and background colors.  
**Those blue shards on the blue bottom of the blue bay wtf!
:slight_smile:** \- system->camera, turn off the water collision and fix the camera above the water looking down and the object outlines pop. Might need to flip gamma and brightness one way or the other too. (I got that one from wowhead comments about a quest in suramar.)
